# package secevent

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus/secevent"
```

Package secevent carries security-relevant observations of a Modbus endpoint to the application: who connected, which connections the server refused and why, how each one ended.

An endpoint (a modbus.Server, through ServerConfig.Security) hands every observation to a Dispatcher as an Event. The dispatcher never blocks the goroutine that observed it: it queues the event, merges repeats of the same kind inside a short window into one event with a count, and calls the application's Sink from a goroutine of its own. When the queue is full the event is dropped and counted, and the next event the sink receives is preceded by a meta.events\_dropped event that says how many were lost; the library never drops silently.

With no Sink and no Dispatcher configured nothing is built, queued or timed: an endpoint without a security policy behaves as it did before this package existed.

Event kinds are part of the API. A Kind is never renamed; the catalogue (Kinds, Describe) gives the default category and severity of each. The kind names that go-iecp5 uses for the same observations (conn.\*, tls.\*, peer.\*, meta.\*) have the same spelling here.

An event describes what the endpoint observed, not what an attacker did: a refused connection may be a scanner or a misconfigured master. Register values and write payloads never appear in Detail.

## Functions

### func NewContext

```go
func NewContext(ctx context.Context, r Reporter) context.Context
```

NewContext returns a context that carries r, for Report and PeerFromContext.

### func NextConnID

```go
func NextConnID() uint64
```

NextConnID returns a new connection identifier: 1, 2, 3, ... for the process, shared by every endpoint, so that the events of one connection can be put together.

### func Report

```go
func Report(ctx context.Context, e Event) bool
```

Report reports e as an event of the connection ctx belongs to, which is the context a RequestHandler method receives. It returns false, and does nothing, when ctx carries no reporter: the server has no security policy with a sink, or ctx is not a handler's.

A handler knows what the library cannot: which addresses exist, which writes are allowed. Detail must hold no register values or payloads.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Sink receives the events. Required.
	Sink Sink
	// QueueSize is the number of events that may wait for the sink; further
	// ones are dropped and counted. Default DefaultQueueSize.
	QueueSize int
	// AggregateWindow is how long repeats of an event are merged into one:
	// the first occurrence is delivered at once, the ones that follow inside
	// the window are counted and delivered together as one event (Count,
	// FirstSeen) when it ends. Zero is DefaultAggregateWindow; a negative
	// value turns merging off.
	AggregateWindow time.Duration
	// MaxAggregateKeys bounds the memory of the merging: when that many
	// distinct events are being merged, the pending count of one is
	// delivered early to make room. Default DefaultMaxAggregateKeys.
	MaxAggregateKeys int
	// MaxRaw is the most bytes of Event.Raw kept. Default DefaultMaxRaw.
	MaxRaw int
	// Logf, when set, is told of a sink that did not return normally
	// (with the stack).
	Logf func(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Config configures a Dispatcher. Zero values take the defaults.

### type Dispatcher

```go
type Dispatcher struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Dispatcher queues events and delivers them to a Sink from a goroutine of its own. Emit never blocks. See the package documentation.

#### func NewDispatcher

```go
func NewDispatcher(cfg Config) (*Dispatcher, error)
```

NewDispatcher starts a dispatcher that delivers to cfg.Sink. Close it when it is no longer needed.

#### func (Dispatcher) Close

```go
func (d *Dispatcher) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close stops the dispatcher accepting events and waits until the ones queued have been delivered, or ctx ends. Called from the sink itself it does not wait (it would wait for itself): the queued events are delivered after the sink returns.

#### func (Dispatcher) CloseNoWait

```go
func (d *Dispatcher) CloseNoWait()
```

CloseNoWait stops the dispatcher accepting events. The events already queued are still delivered, then the goroutine ends. It does not wait.

#### func (Dispatcher) Emit

```go
func (d *Dispatcher) Emit(e Event)
```

Emit hands e to the dispatcher. It never blocks: when the queue is full the event is dropped and counted. Unset Time, Category, Severity, Action, Protocol and Technique are filled in (from the catalogue, for a known kind). It does nothing on a nil or closed dispatcher.

#### func (Dispatcher) OnGoroutine

```go
func (d *Dispatcher) OnGoroutine() bool
```

OnGoroutine reports whether the caller runs on the dispatcher's goroutine, that is, inside the sink.

#### func (Dispatcher) Stats

```go
func (d *Dispatcher) Stats() Stats
```

Stats returns a snapshot of the counters.

### type Event

```go
type Event struct {
	Time     time.Time
	Kind     Kind
	Category Category
	Severity Severity
	Action   Action

	// Protocol is "modbus", Transport "tcp" or "tcp+tls", Role "server".
	Protocol  string
	Transport string
	Role      string
	// ConnID is the identifier of the connection the event belongs to, from
	// NextConnID; it is 0 for events that belong to none.
	ConnID uint64
	Peer   PeerInfo
	Local  string

	// Fields says which of the protocol fields below are set.
	Fields        FieldMask
	UnitID        uint8
	FunctionCode  FunctionCode
	SubFunction   uint16
	Exception     ExceptionCode
	Address       uint16
	Quantity      uint16
	TransactionID uint16
	ExpectedTxnID uint16

	// Count is the number of occurrences the event stands for: 0 or 1 for a
	// single one, more for a merged one (see Dispatcher). FirstSeen is the
	// time of the first occurrence it stands for.
	Count     int
	FirstSeen time.Time

	// Detail is one line of English, with no register values, payloads or
	// key material. Err is the underlying error, when there is one. Raw is a
	// copy of the offending bytes, cut to the dispatcher's MaxRaw.
	Detail string
	Err    error
	Raw    []byte

	// Technique is a MITRE ATT&CK for ICS hint for SIEM routing, not an
	// attribution.
	Technique string
}
```

Event is one observation.

### type Kind

```go
type Kind string
```

Kind names one sort of event, as a stable dotted code such as "conn.rejected\_limit". The values are part of the API and are never renamed.

```go
const (
	// KindConnAccepted: a connection was accepted, before any check on it.
	KindConnAccepted Kind = "conn.accepted"
	// KindConnUnexpected: ServerConfig.AllowClient refused the peer.
	KindConnUnexpected Kind = "conn.unexpected"
	// KindConnRejectedLimit: every ServerConfig.MaxClients slot was taken.
	KindConnRejectedLimit Kind = "conn.rejected_limit"
	// KindConnNoRequest: a connection ended without one request read from it
	// (a connect scan, a probe, a client that never sent).
	KindConnNoRequest Kind = "conn.no_request"
	// KindConnIdleTimeout: a connection that had sent requests was closed
	// for idling for ServerConfig.Timeout.
	KindConnIdleTimeout Kind = "conn.idle_timeout"
	// KindConnClosed: the end of every served connection, with the reason.
	KindConnClosed Kind = "conn.closed"
	// KindConnAcceptError: the listener's Accept failed (no file
	// descriptors left, for example) and the server is retrying.
	KindConnAcceptError Kind = "conn.accept_error"

	// KindTLSHandshakeEvicted: a tcp+tls connection that had not completed
	// its handshake was closed to make room for a newer one.
	KindTLSHandshakeEvicted Kind = "tls.handshake_evicted"

	// KindProtoBadMBAP: the peer sent an MBAP header the server cannot frame
	// (length outside 2..254, protocol identifier other than 0).
	KindProtoBadMBAP Kind = "proto.bad_mbap"
	// KindProtoBadPDU: a request violated the protocol (a PDU whose length
	// does not match its function code).
	KindProtoBadPDU Kind = "proto.bad_pdu"

	// KindDoSWriteStall: a response could not be written within
	// ServerConfig.Timeout (a peer that does not read its answers).
	KindDoSWriteStall Kind = "dos.write_stall"

	// KindMetaEventsDropped: Count events were lost because the queue to the
	// sink was full.
	KindMetaEventsDropped Kind = "meta.events_dropped"
	// KindMetaSinkPanic: the sink did not return normally. Reported once.
	KindMetaSinkPanic Kind = "meta.sink_panic"
)
```

The event kinds an endpoint reports. A kind is never renamed or reused.

### type KindInfo

```go
type KindInfo struct {
	Category Category
	Severity Severity
	// Technique is the MITRE ATT&CK for ICS hint ("" for none).
	Technique string
	// AlwaysDeliver kinds are never merged with their repeats.
	AlwaysDeliver bool
	// MergeByPeer kinds are merged per peer address (the host, not the
	// port) rather than per connection: the connection events, which a
	// connection flood would otherwise turn into one event per connection.
	// The first event of a host in a window keeps its connection id; the
	// merged one carries the last.
	MergeByPeer bool
}
```

### type Policy

```go
type Policy struct {
	// Sink receives the endpoint's events. The endpoint creates a Dispatcher
	// for it when it starts and closes it when it stops. Nil, with no
	// Dispatcher, leaves event delivery off.
	Sink Sink
	// Dispatcher is a dispatcher shared with other endpoints; the endpoint
	// uses it and does not close it. It replaces Sink: set one of the two.
	Dispatcher *Dispatcher

	// QueueSize, AggregateWindow, MaxAggregateKeys and MaxRaw configure the
	// dispatcher created for Sink (see Config); they have no effect on a
	// shared Dispatcher.
	QueueSize        int
	AggregateWindow  time.Duration
	MaxAggregateKeys int
	MaxRaw           int
}
```

Policy is the part of an endpoint's security configuration that does not depend on the protocol. modbus.SecurityPolicy embeds it.

### type Sink

```go
type Sink interface {
	OnEvent(Event)
}
```

Sink receives events. A Dispatcher calls it from one goroutine, one event at a time; it may block briefly, but a slow sink makes the queue fill and events drop. A sink that does not return normally is stopped there and reported once (meta.sink\_panic).

#### func FilterSink

```go
func FilterSink(min Severity, s Sink, categories ...Category) Sink
```

FilterSink returns a Sink that passes on the events of at least severity min and, when categories are given, of one of them.

#### func LoggerSink

```go
func LoggerSink(l Logger) Sink
```

LoggerSink returns a Sink that writes each event to l with the prefix "\[CYBER]": info and notice events at info level, warnings at warn level, alerts and critical events at error level.

#### func MultiSink

```go
func MultiSink(sinks ...Sink) Sink
```

MultiSink returns a Sink that passes every event to each of sinks, in order. One that does not return normally ends the call: the ones after it do not see that event.

type Stats struct {
	// Events counts every event handed to the dispatcher, merged and dropped
	// ones included, by kind and by category.
